tagline: Along the badlands floor, then up to the rim.
intro: About 15 miles south of Watford City the park road turns west off US 85 and runs 14 miles into the North Unit, to a dead end and back. The first half traces the floor of the badlands. Midway it crawls up out of the canyon to River Bend Overlook, and from there it is an easy run along the rim to Oxbow Overlook, where the road stops.

Roosevelt first came to the North Dakota badlands in 1883 to hunt bison. Bison are often in sight from the drive now, at any hour of the day. Twenty of them were brought up from the South Unit in 1962.

moments.title: River Bend Overlook
moments.text: The North Unit's best-known view, with a shelter from the Civilian Conservation Corps, whose camps built roads and structures here between 1934 and 1941.

moments.title: Oxbow Overlook
moments.text: The road ends here on the rim, in a unit that is mostly wilderness, set aside by Congress in 1978.

practical: The scenic drive is 28 miles round trip, and the park suggests allowing at least an hour and a quarter. It is almost entirely paved, with one gravel stretch, and is open to RVs and cyclists. There are no services in the park.
